{{nihongo|'''Orihata Shrine'''|織幡神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Chikuzen Province]].

'''Orihata Shrine'' (Orihata Jinja) is located in {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|Q123258|qid=Q123258}}{{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|Q819603|qid=Q819603}}{{ill|Kanezaki|Q11651333|qid=Q11651333|lt=Kanezaki}}.

{{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinai Shrine|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}, and {{ill|Q712534|lt=old shrine rank}} is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}}.

Another name is "Orihataguu". Locals also call him ``Shikihan-sama''.

At the time of ``Munakata Daibosatsu Goengi,'' which was established during the {{ill|Bun'an|Q1193586|qid=Q1193586}} years ({{ill|1444|Q6420|qid=Q6420}}-{{ill|1449|Q6446|qid=Q6446}}), it is written that Minister Takeuchi is the enshrined deity, and {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine )|2000}}, {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}'s ``{{ill|Chikuzen no Kuni Zoku Fudoki|Q108571667|qid=Q108571667}}'' states that the three deities enshrined here are Takeuchi Minister, Sumiyoshi Okami, and Shiga Okami.{{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1978}}. Currently, the eight deities listed above are enshrined, and the three main deities are Takeuchi Minister, Sumiyoshi Okami, and Shiga Okami {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine History Book, Orihata Shrine|2025}}.During the {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}} period, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Honjibutsu}} was considered to be {{ill|Cintāmaṇicakra|Q11446712|qid=Q11446712}} {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}}. {{ill|Munakata Taisha|Q704962|qid=Q704962}} Formerly {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}} {{ill|Chinkoku-ji|Q11651157|qid=Q11651157}}, the original Buddhist statues of the five Munakata shrines (Fukuoka Prefecture-designated cultural properties) including Orihata Shrine have been preserved for generations. <ref>{{PDFlink|[http://city.munakata.lg.jp/w009/050/140/0010/130/13-14shinaisiteibunkazai-shuusei.pdf Cultural properties in the city]}} (Munakata City homepage). </ref>.

=== About the enshrined deity ===
The theory that the enshrined deity of Orihata Shrine is Takeuchi Sukune (Minister Takeuchi) dates back to ``Munakata Daibosatsu Goengi,'' which was established in the middle of the {{ill|15th century|Q7018|qid=Q7018}}, and the same Engi records the founding tradition described below ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sōken-bushi}}). On the other hand, the precincts of Orihata Shrine are located at Cape Kaneno, a strategic point that juts out into the sea, and the entire area is also identified as ``Kaifu-go'' in ``{{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542|lt=Japanese namebook}}'', indicating that Kaifu existed there. Because of its location in the region, there is a theory that it was originally a sea god worshiped by the Kaijin tribe. As mentioned below ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=tradition section}}), "{{ill|Man'yōshū|Q834321|qid=Q834321}}" <ref group="Hara" name="Manyoshu"/>When passing Cape Kaneno, there is a shrine called "Shiga no Kojin" ({{ill|Shikaumi Shrine|Q11491171|qid=Q11491171}}Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Aduji|Q3377806} }There is also a theory that the Azumi clan (Adu tribe), a member of the Kaijin tribe, resided in the area and worshiped the Shiga god, as there is a song that says they pray to the god Hosai.{{Sfn|Kanasaki/Kanezaki (Heibonsha)|2004}}Also, "{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}" {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}} era<ref group="Hara" name="Emperor Ojin 37th year">"Nihon Shoki" Article dated February 1, 1997 of Emperor Ojin, article of February 41, 41st year of Emperor Ojin. In </ref>, the Emperor ordered {{ill|Achi no Omi|Q11657596|qid=Q11657596}} and {{ill|Tuka Messenger|Q24863564|qid=Q24863564}} to go to Wu (Kangnan, China) and obtain sewing women, but when the Achi Messengers returned home, they were told that they had ``Chunkagata Okami'' (= There is a legend that he offered his older brother among the four female factory workers to the god Munakata Okami) at the request of the god Munakata Okami. </ref>, there is also a theory that connects this tradition with Orihata Shrine. Among these theories, it is pointed out that the weavers who weave clothes to offer to the gods may have been deified.{{Sfn|Munakata City History In General History Volume 2 | 1999 | pp=31-33}}, it is pointed out that Takeuchi Sukune may have been chosen as the enshrined deity as the common ancestor of the imported clans that were responsible for weaving {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Gods) | 2000}}.Of the eight deities enshrined, Maneko Iki is said to be the founder of the {{ill|Iki clan|Q11429628|qid=Q11429628}}, the former chief priest of Orihata Shrine {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Shikiuchi)|1978}}. In addition to the existence of the Iki clan, the "Otenaga" that appears in the "Munakata Daibosatsu Engi" is {{ill|Iki Island|Q494914|qid=Q494914}}'s Shikinai Shrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amante Nagao Shrine}}・Since it is also associated with Amante Nagahime Shrine, there is a theory that suggests a relationship between the rituals at Orihata Shrine and Iki Island.{{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}.

In addition, there are different theories about the deity enshrined, such as the theory that it is Oomikutsu no Kami, and the theory that it is Kureori or Anaori.{{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Gods)|2000}}.

=== History ===
[[File:Kanezaki Port 01.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Distant view of Cape Kanezaki}}{{small|View from Kanezaki fishing port. Orihata Shrine is located halfway up Mt. Sayagata on the far left of the image. }}]]

=== Founding ===
Regarding its founding, according to "Munakata Daibosatsu Goengi" (established in the mid-15th century), during the {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} {{ill|Three Han Campaign|Q11249435|qid=Q11249435}}, the Minister of Munakata ({{jal ink|Munakata Taisha|Q704962}}) fought with two red and white flags woven by Minister Takeuchi ({{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}}) attached to a flagpole called ``Otenaga'', and in the end, they were used as ``Soku Mishima (= It was built on {{ill|Okinoshima (Fukuoka)|Q7082047|qid=Q7082047}}). At the time of Minister Takeuchi's funeral, the spirit was enshrined on the seashore to protect the sea route from invading pirates, and it was named ``Orihata (Orihata)'' because Minister Takeuchi wove the flag.{{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Shikiuchi)|1978}}{{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}}.

The actual establishment is not known, but as mentioned above, there are theories that suggest a relationship with the Kaijin tribe, {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Kadokawa)|1988}}{{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Gods)|2000}}, "Nihon Shoki" <ref group="Hara" There is a theory that speculates that there is a relationship between {{ill|Achi no Omi|Q11657596|qid=Q11657596}} of name="Emperor Ojin's 37th year"/> and the legend of the seamstress of the Munakata deity.{{Sfn|Munakata City History General History Volume 2|1999|pp=31-33}}{{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Gods)|2000}}{{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}}.

Among the place names that appear in "{{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542|lt=Wamyo Sho}}" from the middle of the {{ill|Heian period|ar|فترة هييآن|ast|Periodu Heian|az|Heyan dövrü|bcl|Panahon ni Heian|bg|Хеян|bn|হেইআন যুগ|br|Marevezh Heian|ca|Període Heian|cs|Období Heian|de|Heian-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Χεϊάν|eo|Epoko Heian|es|Período Heian|eu|Heian aroa|fa|دوره هی‌آن|fi|Heian-kausi|fr|Époque de Heian|gl|Período Heian|he|תקופת הייאן|hi|हेआन काल|hr|Heian (razdoblje)|hu|Heian-kor|hy|Հեիան ժամանակաշրջան|id|Zaman Heian|it|Periodo Heian|ja|平安時代|ka|ჰეიანის პერიოდი|ko|헤이안 시대|la|Aevum Heian|lt|Hejano laikotarpis|mn|Хэйан|mr|हियन कालावधी|ms|Zaman Heian|my|ဟဲအိအန်ခေတ်|nl|Heianperiode|nn|Heian|no|Heian-perioden|oc|Epòca d'Heian|pl|Heian|ps|هېيان دوره|pt|Período Heian|ro|Perioada Heian|ru|Период Хэйан|sh|Heianski period|simple|Heian period|sk|Obdobie Heian|sl|Obdobje Heian|sq|Periudha Heian|sr|Хеиан период|sv|Heian|ta|ஹையன் காலகட்டம்|th|ยุคเฮอัง|tl|Panahong Heian|tr|Heian Dönemi|uk|Період Хейан|vi|Thời kỳ Heian|war|Panahon Heian|wuu|平安时代|zh|平安时代|zh_classical|平安朝|zh_min_nan|Heian sî-tāi|zh_yue|平安時代|qid=Q193292}} According to one theory, this area is located in Kaifu-go, Munakata District. It is presumed that around this Heian period, Orihata Shrine became a shrine under the jurisdiction of Munakata Shrine.According to the Dajokan Code draft of {{ill|Bun'ei|Q1010103|qid=Q1010103}} 2nd year ({{ill|1265|Q5516|qid=Q5516}}), at that time the {{jali nk|Chinkokuji|Q11651157}} {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Honjibutsu}} of ``Kanezaki Orihata Myojin'' was enshrined {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Shikiuchi)|1978}}{{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}}. Also, in the {{ill|kishōmon|Q11636131|qid=Q11636131}} of Bun'ei 9 ({{ill|1272|Q5524|qid=Q5524}}), ``Orihata Daimyojin'' appears {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}}. Established in {{ill|Bun'an|Q1193586|qid=Q1193586}} ({{ill|1444|Q6420|qid=Q6420}}-{{ill|1449|Q6446|qid=Q6446}}) In ``Munakata Daibosatsu Goengi,'' the five gods of Munakata, plus Orihata Daimyojin and Kōgi Gongen, are collectively called the ``Munakata Five Shrines'' {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}}.After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), {{j alink|Modern shrine ranking system|Q712534}} Ranked as {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}} {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1978 }}, in Meiji 15 ({{ill|1882|Q7812|qid=Q7812}}), {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Showa}}3 ({{ill|1928|Q19715|qid=Q19715}}), it was promoted to {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=prefectural shrine}}{{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1978}}.

In the 10th year of the Meiji era ({{ill|1877|Q7773|qid=Q7773}}), Munakata Shrine (currently Munakata Taisha Shrine) reported it to the government as a separate shrine along with Matohara Shrine, Kodaiji Shrine, Miyajidake Shrine, and others.

=== God level ===
* July 29, 3rd year of {{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}} ({{ill|850|Q30364|qid=Q30364}}), Jugoinoge ("{{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|Q1052905|qid=Q1052905}}") <ref group="Hara" name="Kasho 3rd year">"Japanese Emperor Montoku Annals" July 29th Kasho 3rd year (850) article (see {{Harvnb|Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection}}). </ref> - The spelling is "Orihatakami".
* {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} January 27, 3rd year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), from the lower junior fifth rank to the upper junior fifth rank ("{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}") <ref group="Hara" name="Jōgan 1st year">"Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku" Article dated 27th New Year, Jogan 1st year (859) (see {{Harvnb|Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection}}). </ref> - The spelling is "Orihatakami".
* December 15th, {{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 1st year ({{ill|877|Q23905|qid=Q23905}}), from Jugoinoge {{sub|Mama}} to Shogoikege (``Nihon Sandai Jirroku'') <ref group="Hara" name="Genko 1st year">"Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku" December 15th, Genkei 1st year (877) (see {{Harvnb|Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection}}). </ref> - The name is written as "Orihatakami."

=== Shinto priest ===
The rituals at Orihata Shrine are said to have been carried out by {{ill|Iki clan|Q11429628|qid=Q11429628}} {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Shikiuchi)|1978}}. According to legend, this Iki clan is said to be a descendant of the enshrined deity Maneko Iki, and when the Heike clan fell, they changed their surname from "Iki" to "Irie," but {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Bunkyu}} ({{ill|1863|Q7701|qid=Q7701}}) {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}. After that, the Iki family retired from the position of chief priest of Orihata Shrine in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}18 ({{ill|1943|Q18623|qid=Q18623}}) {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}.

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Orihata-jinja (Munakata), shaden.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Shrine building}}{{small|The main shrine is on the left, and the worship hall is on the right. }}]]The precincts are located halfway up Mt. Sayakata, at the tip of Cape Kaneno, which separates {{ill|Genkai Sea|Q498047|qid=Q498047}} and {{ill|Hibiki Sea|Q11288861|qid=Q11288861}}. A temperate forest has formed within the grounds of Orihata Shrine and on Mt. Sayakata, including more than 10 giant trees of {{ill|Podocarpus macrophyllus|Q165063|qid=Q165063}}, {{ill|Castanopsis|Q1065400|qid=Q1065400}}, {{jalink|Hamanabiwa|Q1258941} 4}}・{{ill|Cinnamomum pedunculatum|Q161335|qid=Q161335}}・{{ill|Viburnum odoratissimum|Q12600081|qid=Q12600081}}・{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Onore}}・{{ill|Neolitsea sericea|Q5792530|qid=Q5792530}}・{{ill|Machilus thunbergii|Q5792073|qid=Q5792073|lt=Tab}}・{{ill|Pittosporum tobira|Q161375|qid=Q161375}}・{{ill|Fatsia japonica|Q203569|qid=Q203569}}・{{ill|Camellia japonica|Q160121|qid=Q160121}}・{{ill|Daphniphyllum macropodum|Q846968|qid=Q846968}}・{{ jalink|Yamamomo|Q311617}}・{{ill|Kadsura japonica|Q1441971|qid=Q1441971}}・{{ill|Piper kadsura|Q5924111|qid=Q5924111}}・{{ill|Cleyera japonica|Q775470|qid=Q775470}}・{{ill|Aucuba japonica|Q163114|qid=Q163114|lt=Aoki}}, {{ill|Euonymus japonicus|Q161383|qid=Q161383}}, {{ill|Marsdenia tomentosa|Q5367121|qid=Q5367121|lt=Kijoorchid}}, and {{ill|Aphananthe aspera|Q4779482|qid=Q4779482}}. This natural forest has been designated as a natural monument of Fukuoka Prefecture as the ``Orihata Shrine Inumaki Natural Forest'' (Munahaku Electronic Museum). </ref>.According to ancient documents, the current main shrine was built in {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}}8 ({{ill|1695|Q7696|qid=Q7696}}), and the worship hall was built in Genroku 16 ({{ill|1703|Q6822|qid=Q6822}}). Several other companies are also located within the precincts.

Also within the precincts are Kutsuzuka, where the enshrined deity, Minister Takeuchi, buried the shoe left after ascending to heaven, {{Sfn|Orihata Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}, and a huge stone related to the legend of the sinking bell, which will be described later.

* Natural monument

=== Tradition ===
[[File:Orihata-jinja (Munakata), kyoseki.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Giant stone of the legend of the sunken bell}}]]
There is a legend that a foreign bell is sunk in the sea at Cape Kanenomisaki, where Orihata Shrine is located. The place name ``Cape Kaneno'' comes from this, and similar legends of sinking bells are known all over the country, but this area and Kanegasaki in {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|Q133879|qid=Q133879}} are especially famous <ref name="Complete Works of Japanese Classical Literature"/>. However, what was thought to be a bell on the sea floor at Cape Kaneno was brought back to land in {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}}8 ({{ill|1919|Q2157|qid=Q2157}}), but what was pulled up at that time was not a bell but a megalith<ref name="Explanation board"/>. This megalith is currently enshrined on the approach to Orihata Shrine.

Additionally, the area between Cape Kaneno and {{ill|Jinoshima|Q17992764|qid=Q17992764}} on the opposite shore is a reef area, and it is known that it has been a key point and difficult point for maritime transportation since ancient times. "{{ill|Man'yōshū|Q834321|qid=Q834321}}" <ref group="Hara" name="Manyoushu">Manyoushu volume 7 number 1230 ([http://infux03.inf.edu.yamaguchi-u.ac.jp/~manyou/ver2_2/manyou_kekka2.php?kekka=07/1230 07/1230] <Yamaguchi University "Man'yoshu Search System"> reference). </ref>So,{{Cquote|Chihayaburu Even if I don't pass the golden cape, I won't forget Shiga's Emperor (Sumekami)|20px||"{{ill|Man'yōshū|Q834321|qid=Q834321}}" Volume 7 No. 1230<ref name="Complete Works of Japanese Classical Literature">"New Edition of Japanese Classical Literature Complete Works 7 Man'yoshu (2)” Shogakukan, 2004 ({{ill|JapanKnowledge|Q11309996|qid=Q11309996}} edition), pp. 226-227. </ref>}}
There is a song about praying to the god of the sea when passing Cape Kaneno (Kin no Misaki) {{Sfn|Kanasaki/Kanezaki (Heibonsha)|2004}}. Based on this song, there is a theory that Cape Kanenosaki was once inhabited by the Azum tribe, who worshiped the god Shiga. {{Sfn|Kanasaki/Kanezaki (Heibonsha)|2004}}.
